data.title: Former Nvidia executive under scanner over sale of servers to China
data.description:
After Jensen Huang, former Nvidia top executive Jay Puri's relationship with senior tech executive Cenly Chen is under the scanner amid a US investigation into the alleged diversion of the company's servers to China.

Puri, who previously led Nvidia's global sales operations, and Chen, Super Micro's former chief growth officer, dated for several years before marrying on March 7, 2026, the Wall Street Journal reported.

Puri's professional association with Chen has drawn attention because he oversaw Nvidia's global sales and chip allocation. Chen worked closely with the server maker's customers and had regular dealings with Nvidia.

"I never had to rely on personal relationships for professional gain," Chen told the Journal by email.

 

The Journal said Nvidia and Puri did not respond to its requests for comment. Chen now runs AI computing provider ChronoScale.

Puri stepped down as Nvidia's executive vice president of worldwide field operations. Nvidia said in a July securities filing that it expected him to stay on in a senior advisory role to help his successor, Nick Parker, take over.

Super Micro, meanwhile, told WSJ that Chen "did not manage Supermicro's overall relationship with Nvidia or our procurement of Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs)". It said that a process involving several departments determined how the company allocated Nvidia chips to its customers.

On March 19, the US Justice Department announced charges against a Super Micro co-founder, a sales manager and a third-party broker. They were accused of conspiring to smuggle more than USD 500 million worth of servers containing advanced Nvidia chips into China.

The investigation also involves allegations that servers worth $2.5 billion were sold to Chinese customers through a Singapore-based front company.

The FBI has reportedly questioned a person familiar with Super Micro and sought information about senior executives, including Chen.

The report comes as Nvidia deals with revelations about co-founder Huang's extramarital affair with an executive at Megaspeed International.

That executive is suspected by some US officials of having worked with Chinese intelligence. Huang resigned from NVIDIA but returned as CEO this week, after US President Donald Trump intervened with the company's board.

data.title: IIFCL, UCO Bank eye debut dollar debt before RBI window shuts, say bankers
data.description:
State-run financiers India Infrastructure Finance Company (IIFCL) and UCO Bank plan to ​issue debut dollar-denominated bonds next month before the central bank's subsidised swap window closes, two merchant bankers said on Friday.
 
The plans come as US Treasury yields slide amid an unravelling of the global AI trade and investors ‌flocking towards safe-haven assets, making the window, ​which closes on December 31, ​more attractive.
 
IIFCL could raise around $500 million through a five-year debt issue, ​while UCO Bank could add to the $1 billion fundraising it has already approved with a smaller size of around $250 million-$300 million maturing in three or five years, the bankers said.
 
 
The bankers requested anonymity ​as the matters are still private, while IIFCL and UCO Bank ‌did not reply to Reuters emails for comments.
 
Some Indian firms had ​earlier pushed back their plans after a spike in Treasury yields made borrowing more expensive, the bankers said.
 
IIFCL recently held meetings with investors as part ‌of a non-deal road show ​and received a BBB long-term ‌rating from S&P earlier this month.
 
The debt of UCO Bank is ‌rated BBB by S&P and BBB- by Fitch Ratings.
 
In June, the ​Reserve Bank of India announced measures to stabilise the rupee, including a subsidised hedging facility for lenders and state-run ​firms to lower their overall borrowing costs.
 
Indian lenders have so far raised $13 billion under the scheme.
 
In September, National ‌Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development raised dollar debt worth $750 million through 10-year ‌papers at 6.1220%, or at a spread of 105 basis points above comparable US yields.
 
Power Finance Corp also raised $300 million through three-year bonds at a spread of 110 bps over US Treasuries.

data.title: Zaggle up 7% from day's low on inking deal with Yokohama, WSFX Global Pay
data.description:
Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services rebounded by 5.8 per cent from the day's low of ₹157.50 in Friday's intraday deals after the company announced signing a forex services agreement. The stock hit an intraday high of ₹168.18 on the NSE. At 1:45 PM, Zaggle pared gains and traded on a flat note at ₹162.67 on trades of around 40 lakh shares on the NSE. The stock hit a 52-week low at ₹146.65 on October 26, 2026, and a 52-week high of ₹397 was registered on November 28, 2025. Zaggle stock has witnessed a significant downturn since hitting a record high of ₹592 in September 2024. At current levels, the stock trades over 72 per cent lower compared to its peak, and down 53 per cent on a year-till-date basis. 

Zaggle inks 'Tripartite Agreement' with Yokohama and WSFX Global Pay

Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services in an exchange filing on Friday, said the company entered into a tripartite agreement with Yokohama Private Limited (Customer) and WSFX Global Pay Limited (WSFX). 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Shriram Fin, Bajaj Auto lead 700-pt loss in Sensex; Nifty below 25,700
 
 According to the terms of the agreement, Zaggle shall provide Expense Management System (EMS) to Yokohama, while WSFX shall act as the Authorised Dealer for forex services to Yokohama. Revenue from the agreement is variable in nature, and shall be in force for one year, unless terminated earlier. "The Quantum of fees is subjected to the number of international transactions made by the employees of the customer for the respective months on the Platform. "In such a case it would be difficult to ascertain the value/amount of the contract at this stage," Zaggle said in its release. Vijay Kedia bought stake in August Kedia Securities, owned by veteran investor Vijay Kishanlal Kedia, acquired 20 lakh shares, representing a 1.48 per cent stake in Zaggle in August. Kedia bought 20 lakh equity shares at ₹164.72 per share, for an aggregate consideration of approximately ₹32.94 crore. Equirus Securities has 'Long' rating on Zaggle Equirus Securities has a 'Long' rating on Zaggle with a price target of ₹275 per share by March 2028. The brokerage said, Zaggle's Q2FY27 revenue execeded its estimate by 2.8 per cent, while Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (Ebitda) was in line. Zaggle's management expects EBITDA margins of 7-8 per cent and continue to prioritise cash conversion and disciplined capitalisation. "Around 65-70 per cent of DICE contracts have been novated, with the remaining transfers expected in 3QFY27. We see Zaggle well positioned to benefit from wider adoption of spend management solutions, while acquisitions strengthen client stickiness," said the brokerage. Even as Equirus maintained a 'Long' rating, the brokerage cut FY27/FY28 earnings estimates by 13.4 per cent/6.2 per cent citing moderate programme fee growth and the near-term profitability drag from DICE integration. "We expect technology expenses, DICE integration and Zagg.money losses to weigh on near-term margins and model a 7.8 per cent EBITDA margin for FY27E,", the brocaded added. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. data.title: Union Cabinet clears fresh women's quota bill linked to delimitation
data.description:
The Union Cabinet met here on Friday and is learnt to have cleared a fresh delimitation-linked women's reservation bill, which is likely to be brought before the special sitting of Parliament beginning next week.

Sources said the bill was brought before the special meeting of the Union Cabinet, which is expected to accord its nod to the fresh bill with some amendments to ensure that no state loses its representation in the Lok Sabha in proportion to other states after delimitation.

The Cabinet meeting was chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and was convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth to discuss the bill, which the government is keen to get passed in the special sitting of Parliament starting Monday.

 

The bill was brought in Parliament by the government during a special sitting in April, but it could not pass muster in the Lok Sabha.

The government has now claimed that it has the numbers to get the legislation through.

A two-thirds majority in both houses of Parliament is a must for a Constitutional amendment bill to get cleared.

Sources said the DMK and NCP, besides BRS, are expected to support the bill.

The opposition INDIA bloc is against the legislation and will be meeting on Saturday to discuss its strategy.

data.title: Angel One surges 7% on huge volume; stock nears record high in weak market
data.description:
Angel One share price movement

 
Share price of Angel One hit a 52-week high of ₹382.85, soaring 7 per cent on the BSE in Friday’s intraday deals amid heavy volume in an otherwise weak market. Analysts attribute the buying interest at the counter to expectations of a potential recovery in orders alongside growth in the margin trading facility (MTF) book. The stock quoted close to its record high of ₹390.04 touched on January 9, 2024.
 
At 02:20 PM, Angel One was quoting 6 per cent higher at ₹379.90, compared to a 0.85 per cent decline in the BSE Sensex. The average trading volume at the counter jumped over two-fold with a combined 31.03 million shares changing hands on the NSE and BSE.
 
 
In the past month, the stock price of the stock broking & allied services company surged 32 per cent against a 13.6 per cent rally in the BSE Sensex. Further, thus far in the calendar year 2026, Angel One’s market price zoomed 61 per cent compared to a 2 per cent decline in the benchmark index.
 

About Angel One, Q1 results

 
Angel One is one of India’s leading FinTech platforms, transforming how millions invest and build wealth. With a user base of over 40 million, the company offers a wide range of digital-first solutions across broking, credit mutual fund, advisory, wealth and asset management (AMC) and distribution of third-party financial products. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Shriram Fin, Bajaj Auto lead 800-pt loss in Sensex; Nifty below 25,700
 
With a sharp focus on scalable tech, Angel One integrates AI, machine learning and data-driven intelligence to deepen client engagement and retention. The company’s flagship Super App and developer-focused SmartAPI - an open API platform for traders—and Smart Money - a comprehensive investor education platform—are designed to serve users who are mobile-first, data-savvy and growth-driven, the brokerage said in a press release.
 
Angel One's average MTF book grew 21.4 per cent to ₹7,450 crore in September 2026 from ₹6,140 crore in June 2026. Management said the MTF book continues to grow well and remains an important contributor to interest income, as it reached a record period-end high of ₹8,200 crore in Q2FY27.
 
India is witnessing one of the largest wealth creation opportunities in its history, and technology is making financial services more accessible than ever before. Angel One’s management believes the next decade will belong to platforms that combine innovation, trust and execution at scale.
 
Angel One is evolving into an AI-powered financial platform designed to serve clients across trading and investing, wealth, credit and global markets. With strong foundations, multiple growth engines and a relentless focus on client outcomes, the management is confident in the company’s ability to create enduring value while contributing meaningfully to India's financial future.
 
Management sees significant potential in credit distribution. Angel is building this vertical in a disciplined manner with a long-term focus, particularly as it is in an early stage. Currently, only a small fraction of Angel’s client base accesses credit through the platform, which represents a major opportunity, given that these clients already avail over INR 1trn in personal loans annually from the broader market, the release stated.
 

Motilal Oswal Financial Services view on Capital Market

 
India's MTF book has grown over 5x from ₹28,200 crore in April 2022 to ₹1.5 trillion in November 2026, driven by regulatory tightening in derivatives, rising retail participation and increasing broker focus on revenue diversification.
 
Future & Option (F&O) restrictions like peak-margin requirements, higher contract sizes, fewer weekly expiries and increased securities transaction tax (STT); have encouraged retail investors to shift towards leveraged cash-market products. Nearly half the MTF book is deployed in non-F&O stocks, where MTF remains the primary avenue for overnight leveraged exposure.
 
Large discount brokers such as Groww, Zerodha and Angel One are scaling their MTF offerings to diversify beyond transaction-linked broking income, gaining share from bank-backed brokers. Access to low-cost funding, balance-sheet strength and funded client penetration will increasingly drive competitive positioning, Motilal Oswal Financial Services said in its capital market sector report.
 
At 0.3 per cent of market capitalisation, India's MTF penetration remains relatively low versus global markets, providing headroom for growth. MTF offers a structural growth opportunity for brokers and an incremental volume cushion for exchanges, albeit with rising concentration and regulatory risks, the brokerage firm said. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Bosch announces record date for stock split, bonus issue; key details
data.description:
Bosch Ltd has announced the record date for the sub-division (stock split) and bonus issue of equity shares. In an exchange filing on Friday, the company informed that December 23 has been set as the record date for the two corporate actions.
 
The record date will determine the eligibility of shareholders to receive the benefits of both corporate actions.
 
Under the sub-division, Bosch will split its shares of face value of ₹10 into five equity shares with a face value of ₹2 each. 
 
"Sub-division of 1 (one) equity share of face value of ₹10 each fully paid-up into 5 (five) equity shares of face value of ₹2 each fully paid-up," the company had said in a filing earlier this month.
 
 
Post stock split, the company will issue three bonus shares of ₹2 each for every one equity share of ₹2 held by eligible shareholders.
 
"Issue of bonus equity shares in the ratio of 3:1 i.e., 3 (Three) bonus equity shares of face value ₹2 (Rupees Two) each for every 1 (one) equity share of face value ₹2 (Rupees Two) each fully paid up," the filing added.
 
Consequently, Bosch shareholders holding one share will receive a total of 20 shares after the sub-division and bonus issue. 
Bosch sets record date for stock split, bonus issue
 
In other words, the stock split will reduce the face value of each share from ₹10 to ₹2, with shareholders receiving four additional shares for every share held. This will increase the number of shares from one to five. Subsequently, the bonus issue will entitle shareholders to three additional shares for every ₹2 share held after the split. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Shriram Fin, Bajaj Auto lead 600-pt loss in Sensex; Nifty below 25,700
 
Thus, one share of ₹10 face value will translate into 20 shares of ₹2 face value after both corporate actions are completed.
 
The combined effect of the stock split and bonus issue would reduce the share price to one-fifth of its pre-corporate action level. It will not change the overall value of an investor's holding. 
Meanwhile, Bosch Ltd shares traded 1 per cent higher at ₹49,273 on BSE around 2:30 PM.

data.title: Global brands move Bangladesh orders worth millions to India amid unrest
data.description:
Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs in the first half of November, as labour unrest disrupted production and rising costs eroded the country's competitive edge, three factory owners said.
 
Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said, in a shift that represents a major blow to a key pillar of Bangladesh's economy and could extend beyond the current unrest.
 
Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy ‌shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped make Bangladesh the world's second-largest ​apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing.
  
The protests have caused ​more than $400 million in production losses, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in an industry that accounts for more than 80% of Bangladesh's export earnings and nearly 40% ​of its manufacturing jobs.
 
India has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of the order diversions, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery reliability, industry leaders said.
 
Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, though the rise was the smallest in four decades.
 
The increase fell well short of workers' demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, said the wage increase was "satisfactory" ​and that he hoped all garment workers would resume work from Saturday.
 
Industry leaders said the increase would nevertheless narrow Bangladesh's labour-cost advantage over India, although union groups argue the wages remain low by global apparel ‌industry standards.
 
The factory owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and ​other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the bulk of the business.
 
Zara owner Inditex declined to comment on Reuters' questions, while M&S, H&M and Celio did not respond to requests for comment.
 
M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a director of the BGMEA, said higher wages, utility and raw-material costs were adding to pressure on manufacturers.
 
"The wage increase has added to costs at a time when buyers are demanding lower prices and competition ‌from rival sourcing countries is intensifying," he said.
 
Mahmud Hasan Khan, the group's ​president, declined to name the brands but said temporarily shifting some orders elsewhere helps the industry ‌retain global clients while minimising financial losses.
 
MORE BUSINESS AT RISK 
 
Factory owners said the bigger concern was that orders already diverted could be followed by the loss of future business as ‌buyers reassessed where to source garments.
 
Persistent energy shortages, exacerbated by the Middle East crisis, have added to production disruptions and forced some factories to rely on more expensive alternative power ​sources.
 
Chowdhury said buyers were increasingly prioritising delivery times over price when choosing suppliers.
 
"Price becomes secondary when brands are under pressure to meet strict delivery deadlines," he said.
 
India can offer buyers a delivery advantage of about a week, while Vietnam and Cambodia can cut lead times by as ​much as 15 days, Chowdhury said.
 
Rival sourcing hubs can typically complete production and delivery within 60 to 90 days, compared with about 120 days in Bangladesh, he added.
 
The disruptions have also created production backlogs, with manufacturers around Dhaka losing an estimated 20 to 25 production days. Some are considering overtime and costly air freight to meet ‌delivery commitments.
 
Khan Monirul Alam, managing director of Alps Apparels Group, which mainly supplies European brands, said the unrest was already hitting new business.
 
"Since November 1, most of my buyers have stopped ‌placing orders because of the unrest," Alam said. "They are telling us our orders have been shifted, postponed or cancelled and that they have already found alternative solutions."
 
Political tensions surrounding former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's possible return to Dhaka from India have added to concerns about further disruption.
 
Industry leaders said restoring stability and uninterrupted production would be critical to retaining international buyers. Chowdhury warned that orders shifted elsewhere during periods of instability might not return even after conditions improved.
 
"The challenge is restoring buyers' confidence before temporary shifts become long-term sourcing decisions," he said. "Brands have options. They will not wait for us ​if instability persists."

data.title: Bangladesh minister says Hasina is a 'thorn' in bilateral ties with India
data.description:
Sheikh Hasina has become a "thorn" in Bangladesh-India relations, with New Delhi beginning to realise the strain her presence in the country is causing to bilateral ties, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir has said.

Comparing the deposed prime minister to an unwelcome guest who suddenly walks into someone's home, Kobir said India is in a difficult position as it could neither send her away nor avoid dealing with her presence, news portal bdnews24 reported.

"Hasina has become a thorn in Bangladesh-India relations," he told reporters at the foreign ministry on Thursday.

"She has become an irritation, and they understand that this is a problem for the relationship," Kobir said.

 

His remarks came a day after India refrained from commenting on Hasina's plan to return to Bangladesh on December 16.

External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal on Wednesday said that her voluntary return should be treated separately from Dhaka's extradition request, which New Delhi is examining through established legal processes.

Kobir reiterated that Hasina could return only under the extradition treaty between India and Bangladesh, either in handcuffs or under strict surveillance.

"She is a criminal. There is one policy for criminals and another for ordinary citizens. She falls under the criminal category. She will come only through the extradition treaty. It is not a matter of her returning; she will be handed over," he said.

Hasina's presence in India has emerged as a contentious issue in bilateral ties since her departure from Bangladesh.

She faces serious legal challenges in her home country, including a death sentence handed down in absentia by a special tribunal over the deadly crackdown on protesters during the uprising in 2024.

Hasina has denied wrongdoing and questioned the legitimacy of the proceedings.

Her spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali on Tuesday said that the 79-year-old ousted premier plans to return home on December 16, the day the country celebrates its victory over Pakistan in the 1971 Liberation War.

Hasina, the daughter of Bangladesh's founding leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, ruled the country for 15 years before her ouster.

India had enjoyed close relations with Hasina during her 15 years in power and hoped that the formation of a new government in Bangladesh would provide an opportunity to reset ties, which deteriorated sharply after her ouster.

However, since taking office in February, Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman is yet to visit India despite an invitation. He skipped the BRICS summit hosted by India in September.

data.title: India's power sector needs ₹200 trillion investments by 2047: Manohar Lal
data.description:
India's power sector will need investments to the tune of ₹200 trillion until 2047 to achieve various targets, Union minister Manohar Lal said on Friday, and called for stock market listings of state-owned firms and participation from private players to raise funds.

Speaking at the Power Ministers' Conference of States and Union Territories here, Lal emphasised the need for the Centre and states to work as a team to tackle challenges related to transmission of renewable energy.

The power minster also said that the total loss of discoms across the country has reached ₹7 trillion again, even after the central government absorbed about the same amount of losses in 2017 through UDAY (Ujjwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana), a financial package scheme for revival of power distribution companies (discoms).

 

"We absorbed about ₹7 trillion loss under the UDAY scheme in 2017. Losses of discoms of the entire nation have again reached ₹7 trillion," he said.

He also pointed out that last year, all discoms together earned a profit of ₹2,600 crore.

Now the challenge is that we should not turn this profit into a loss again, he said and suggested the states to use these profits to set off losses incurred earlier.

"We need to ensure that the financial position of our DISCOMs is strengthened and necessary changes in policy, operations and regulation should facilitate the continuation of this turnaround," he said.

About the investment opportunity in the power sector, he said, "There will be investment of ₹200 trillion to meet fixed targets in the power sector only by 2047, which is equal to five years' budget of the government. We cannot do this investment alone. We need investments from the public and list our public sector firms as well as investment of private sector under the public-private partnership." Prime Minister Narendra Modi has recently stated that 500 GW more renewable energy would be added in the next 10 years.

Today we have 300 GW of installed renewable energy capacity, he noted.

For expanding the power transmission network, the Centre and states would need to work as 'Team India', he said, as he highlighted the lack of transmission network, especially for renewable energy, and said there is problem or issues in evacuation of solar power.

It is not a good situation that there is huge generation of power but there is a lack of transmission network to evacuate that, he said.

He further said that the power demand will increase due to expanding data centre infrastructure and increased usage of electric vehicles.

There is a need to focus on storage for optimum use of solar and other renewable sources, he said and urged states to encourage use of solar energy for agriculture and generation of electricity through rooftop solar.

He also highlighted that there are shortcomings in tariff, coordination and regulation (of tariff) of renewable energy sources, saying the regulation should be such that the discoms should not suffer losses.

The minister invited suggestions to add energy storage capacities, advocated the use of advanced technologies like pre-paid smart meters and AI tools to improve delivery, and asked states to clear pending electricity bills of government establishments and official residences to set the precedent.

He also asked states to focus on nuclear power for clean source of energy for the future.

The two-day power conference began on Friday. The last such conference at the national level was held in 2024.

According to a power ministry statement, the conference will comprise interactions and in-depth discussions among the Ministry of Power, states and other stakeholders on key issues such as implementation of resource adequacy plans, including accelerated energy storage deployment; inter-state and intra-state transmission issues; financial viability of discoms, implementation of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with emphasis on smart metering, feeder separation and household electrification; and issues related to nuclear sites.

Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State for Power, asked the participating states and UTs to share their experiences, including difficulties in implementation, regulatory issues and areas where further support or intervention from the central government may be required.

"Our collective focus should be on moving from policy formulation to effective execution, from infrastructure creation to measurable outcomes, and from individual interventions to an integrated and sustainable power sector", Naik said.

Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal noted that the core guidance received from the Prime Minister is to move beyond energy security toward true energy independence in service of Viksit Bharat@2047.

The past year has been one of record growth, he said, and noted that India's installed capacity is now about 563 GW, and more than 55 per cent of it is non-fossil.

In the last 12 months, around 60 GW of capacity was added, 87 per cent of it from non-fossil sources, he said.

On November 28, the conference will have a joint session with the Forum of Regulators and State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs).

data.title: EPF account inactive for 3 years? Know when interest stops and how to claim
data.description:
An account with no fresh contributions does not automatically stop earning interest after three years. The rules depend on the member's age and circumstances.
 
An Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) account does not automatically become inoperative if no contributions have been credited for three years. For employees who leave a job before turning 55, their accumulated provident fund savings can continue to earn interest until they turn 58, subject to the applicable rules.
 
The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has recently urged subscribers to check whether their accounts have become inoperative and understand the rules governing interest accrual, withdrawals and transfers. Its communication on November 24 also directed members to an explanatory video on the subject.
 
 
The clarification is important for employees who switch jobs, take a career break or leave the workforce, as they may mistakenly believe their old PF account has stopped earning interest after three years.
 

When does an EPF account become inoperative?

Under the EPF rules, an account is classified as inoperative in specific circumstances, rather than simply because contributions have stopped for three years.
 
These include:
 
Retirement after 55: If a member retires after attaining 55 years and does not claim the balance within 36 months, the account can become inoperative.
 
Permanent migration abroad: An account can become inoperative if the member permanently settles abroad and does not claim the money within the prescribed period.
 
Death of a member: If nominees or legal heirs do not claim the accumulated amount within 36 months.
 
Failed payment: If a settlement amount is returned because of incorrect or outdated bank details and remains unclaimed for 36 months.
 
The rules governing inoperative accounts are laid down under the EPF Scheme. The EPFO has clarified that interest on an operative account can continue until the member turns 58, subject to applicable provisions.
 

Does an inoperative account mean your money is lost?

 
No. An inoperative account does not mean the accumulated PF money is forfeited.
 
The balance remains claimable after the member completes the required verification and submits the appropriate application. However, interest is not credited once an account becomes inoperative.
 
Members should therefore avoid leaving their PF savings unattended, particularly if they have changed jobs and have not transferred their accumulated balance.
 
How to withdraw or transfer your PF balance
Members can access their EPF savings through the EPFO Member e-Sewa portal. Before filing a claim, they should check whether their Aadhaar, bank account details and other KYC information are updated and verified.
 

The process involves the following steps:

 
Withdraw the balance: Submit Form 19 online through the EPFO portal for final settlement, subject to eligibility.
 
Transfer the balance: If you have joined another EPF-covered employer, submit Form 13 to transfer the accumulated savings to the new PF account instead of withdrawing them.
 
Claim after death: Nominees or legal heirs can submit the applicable claim forms, including Form 20, subject to the relevant rules.
 
Transferring the balance when changing jobs can help maintain continuity in retirement savings and preserve the benefits associated with long-term EPF accumulation.
 
Members can log in to the EPFO Member e-Sewa portal using their Universal Account Number (UAN) and password to check their balance, update details and initiate claims.
 
The first step for anyone with an old PF account should be to check the balance and account details before deciding whether to withdraw or transfer the money.
